title: Starting clarinet in Boston, after trombone
summary: Lovett began clarinet at 15-16 after a few months of trombone, took legitimate lessons, and improvised jazz from the start.

story.theme_name: Growing up and learning music: family, first instruments, teachers
story.community_name: Picking up the first horn: clarinet and saxophone beginnings

blocks.x: Bob, when did you start playing clarinet? Probably when I was about 16, maybe 15 years old. That would have been around 1940 or 41. Where were you at the time? At that time I was in Boston, Massachusetts. Do you remember what influenced you to be interested in the clarinet? Yes, I was interested in jazz at that time. I had bought quite a few records. I had heard some Louis Armstrong records. In those days I wasn't very discriminating in my taste and I just sort of liked jazz in general.
Was there anything about the clarinet that also attracted you?
Actually, I played trombone before I played clarinet. But for some reason or other I couldn't seem to get with the trombone. I switched after a few months to clarinet. I don't remember exactly why.
Yes, I took some lessons from time to time with different legitimate clarinet teachers.
Did you take lessons on trombone?
This was all legitimate in spite of your jazz interest. You hadn't tried to get lessons in jazz immediately.
Oh no, no. But I experimented playing jazz from as soon as I started playing the clarinet at all.
